content:
nina (Finance): Heads-up: next month were consolidating the per-minute free credits into a single monthly free allotment and introducing an optional purchasable "surge buffer". Goal is to simplify invoices and make short traffic spikes predictable.

jamie (Product): tl;dr: free credits per minute -> single monthly free minutes pool (defaults unchanged for existing customers), and a paid surge buffer customers can buy in Billing Settings to avoid immediate rate-limited errors on short bursts.

kartik (SRE): Clarify rate-limits: were not raising base rate-limits. The surge buffer will be a separate capacity bucket applied by the router as a soft cushion; when it exhausts requests get 429s as usual.

leah (Support): How will this appear on invoices? Customers get worried when new line items pop up.

nina (Finance): Invoice change: new line item "surge_buffer_purchase" (if bought) + a single consolidated "monthly_free_minutes" row. No retroactive changes. Well include an example PDF in the KB.

rafa (Sales): Any discounts for Reserved/Dedicated customers? We should give field guidance for renewals.

nina (Finance): Dedicated and Enterprise customers: default migration keeps behavior identical. Sales can opt them into negotiated buffer pricing; this is mostly for self-serve customers.

jamie (Product): Migration plan: existing self-serve accounts keep their current per-minute credits for 90 days. After grace, we auto-migrate them to an equivalent monthly allotment (calculated from trailing 30d). We'll send 30/14/7 day notices.

kartik (SRE): Implementation notes: router will check surge_buffer flag + amount on org metadata. Buffer is consumed in token-equivalent units. We'll add telemetry to track buffer hits and exhaustion.

billing-bot: deploy started: billing-api:v4.0.0 -> canary (5%)  runbook: /runbooks/surge-buffer-rollout

leah (Support): Draft support blurb: "We've simplified free credits and added an optional surge buffer to help cover short traffic spikes. Existing customers are unaffected for 90 days. See KB for examples and migration steps." Feedback?

jamie (Product): Add a short FAQ entry: What if I don't buy a buffer? Answer: nothing changes functionally; you may see 429s during spikes once your free allotment is used.

nina (Finance): Pricing for the buffer: tiered blocks (100k, 1M, 5M token-equivalents). Billing granularity: charged at time of purchase as a standard invoice line item.

rafa (Sales): For trials and startups, can we auto-apply a small trial buffer? Sales/SDR asked for that.

nina (Finance): We'll offer a one-time complimentary 50k buffer for trial orgs created in the next 60 days. We'll track uptake.

kartik (SRE): Observability: adding a dashboard tile for "buffer consumption rate" and alerts when >80% of canary orgs see buffer exhaustion.

jamie (Product): Communication plan: 1) public blog post with examples, 2) KB with migration calculator, 3) console banner 30 days before migration for affected orgs.

billing-bot: deploy success: billing-api:v4.0.0 canary -> healthy on 5% (2026-03-23T18:12:04Z)

nina (Finance): Legal checked the wording: no change to SLA or dispute windows. Were just adding purchasable buffers; refunds follow existing billing disputes process.

leah (Support): We'll prep canned responses and a small internal playbook for revoke/refund requests.

jamie (Product): OK team, aim to open the beta purchase option to 10% of self-serve orgs next week. If you want to be on the internal test cohort, DM me.

nina (Finance): Thanks all  will send final comms schedule after the beta metrics land."
